gates.title: Gate 0 Freeze the experiment and remove stale assumptions
gates.scope_note: Historical v01 component pass preserved. A revised numerical update must repeat applicable mechanics and topology controls; not inherited physical cutting qualification.

gates.title: Gate 1 Establish trustworthy intact mechanics
gates.scope_note: Historical intact mechanics preserved. v09 GPU matches v07 integrated block forces and short trajectories at primary/half timesteps; no arbitrary tomato/contact qualification. v17 passes initial analytical, CPU/GPU, conservation and selected timestep controls in small linear-element blocks; no inherited tomato/contact qualification. V19 approved weighted-velocity component checks and strict GPU equivalence pass. This does not qualify physical contact, arbitrary-path cutting or a tomato. V20 preserves the tested numerical model while improving local geometric updates, setup and force assembly; strict component and changing-loop comparisons pass, without physical contact/fracture qualification. V21 compiled geometry and persistent GPU storage pass restricted component and changing-loop comparisons; no inherited physical-cut qualification. V22 cached surfaces/operators and independent pipelining preserve the tested numerical model; component speed only, no new physical-cut qualification.

gates.title: Gate 2 Prove persistent cuts on a small block
gates.scope_note: v14 consistent local band and event-localized release passes short action/probe/timestep comparisons, including a faster held-out motion and loaded restart. Restricted single-plane band only. Spatial convergence, growing/moving band, arbitrary paths/full cut and Gate 2 as a whole remain unqualified. v16 local approximation fails oblique cut strain-rank checks; increasing uniform sampling did not resolve every case. No general-path pass. v17 removes the tested angled-cut rank defects and passes four geometric cut fixtures, bridge/independence/restart controls. These are prescribed geometry tests, not physical blade fracture or a finished Gate 2. v18 passes 62 algebra/component checks and eight initial projection cases, but cut-region dynamic response differs beyond the frozen tolerance even after timestep refinement. No physical blade or general-path qualification is inherited. V19 approved weighted-velocity component checks and strict GPU equivalence pass. This does not qualify physical contact, arbitrary-path cutting or a tomato. V20 preserves the tested numerical model while improving local geometric updates, setup and force assembly; strict component and changing-loop comparisons pass, without physical contact/fracture qualification. V21 compiled geometry and persistent GPU storage pass restricted component and changing-loop comparisons; no inherited physical-cut qualification. V22 cached surfaces/operators and independent pipelining preserve the tested numerical model; component speed only, no new physical-cut qualification.

gates.title: Gate 3 Establish cutting resistance and reliable contact
gates.scope_note: Physical blade contact/reaction and irreversible fracture-work remain pending. v14 resolves the prior short-window update comparison in a restricted band but does not complete Gate 2 or establish a physical tomato cut. V23 couples unchanged CAD/contact laws to affine FEM mechanics; 59 operator/geometry/work checks pass and a selected temporal refinement passes. Spatial force refinement fails near release; no paid physical topology event. Full Gate 3 remains incomplete.

gates.title: Gate 4 Build the reusable tomato and complete one slice
Gate 5 Verify freedom to change the cutting technique
Gate 6 Measure interactive and RL performance
gates.scope_note: v15 profiles unchanged v14 tiny block; fixed-topology dynamics already far below the project speed targets. This early no-go does not assert completion of physical prerequisites or a full Gate 6 RL benchmark. v16 bulk-only best 46.61 equivalent steps/s is below 100/s and excludes evolving cuts/contact. No complete environment or RL qualification. v17 first cost gate fails: 65.04/s at intact timestep, 8.27/s at corner-cut timestep, bulk only. History update overhead measured separately. No further candidate expansion. v18 stops earlier at Stage A response accuracy; aggregate GPU throughput is not measured or claimed. V19 approved weighted-velocity component checks and strict GPU equivalence pass. This does not qualify physical contact, arbitrary-path cutting or a tomato. V19 best fixed-topology rates 99-111 equivalent steps/s, with ~1.1-1.5 s CPU geometry/aggregation events excluded; full RL entry target not passed. V20 preserves the tested numerical model while improving local geometric updates, setup and force assembly; strict component and changing-loop comparisons pass, without physical contact/fracture qualification. Full measured geometric diagnostic: 6.04 to 2.72 s wall per 0.2 s sim, one body. Batched material-only rates 124-159/s are not complete environment rates. V21 compiled geometry and persistent GPU storage pass restricted component and changing-loop comparisons; no inherited physical-cut qualification. Eight independent event streams with four host workers achieve ~17 diagnostic transitions/s including geometry/reset/output, but excluding blade/fracture/robot/policy; no RL pass. V22 cached surfaces/operators and independent pipelining preserve the tested numerical model; component speed only, no new physical-cut qualification. Eight repeated 16-environment episodes exceed 100/s with resets and current geometry updates; physical blade/fracture/robot/policy are excluded, so actual RL gate stays pending. V23 dense physical contact on a 6 mm coupon takes ~10.54 s for 13 ms simulation, excluding setup; not a complete RL benchmark and not an equal-resolution comparison to v22. Physical contact speed and accuracy remain unresolved.

gates.title: Gate 7 Connect the existing robot and verify resets
Gate 8 Prepare a small learning demonstration
